author: RichardMCNgo
text:
Love-words which would be useful to import from the Greek:
 - agape (or the Buddhist mettā, maybe?): selfless, unconditional compassion
 - ludus: playful, flirtatious love (because "puppy love" has slightly negative connotations)
 - philia: "brotherly" love for friends

author: RichardMCNgo
text: I wonder if our emotional lives could be improved with better terminology, so that we're forced to be more aware of what exactly we're feeling. For example, the distinction the Ancient Greeks drew between varieties of love. What other emotions do we need words for?

author: RichardMCNgo
text:
Malthusianism is underrated. It:
 - applied during most of human history
 - inspired Darwin
 - was a good prediction at the time
 - is mathematically non-trivial
 - might well hold true for most of humanity's future, as @robinhanson argues, e.g. in https://t.co/3a3U4GH1HT

author: RichardMCNgo
text: Always assume that your explanations are less clear than they seem; that other people's disagreements with you are more reasonable than they seem; and that people spend far less time thinking about you and far more time thinking about their own insecurities than you expect.

quoted.text:
A corollary to Gell-Mann amnesia:

In dialogue with people I often realize they've misunderstood my point the 1st (or 2nd, or 3rd) time I try to express it

But then when I'm writing a talk / article / etc. I just blithely assume everyone will understand the whole thing perfectly

author: RichardMCNgo
text: @gmiller I'm still confused by this. Consider seeing something then moving your leg. Response time = time from eyes to brain + processing time + time from brain to leg. With brain in chest, the first is longer but the last is shorter. (Even more so when it's leg nerve->brain->leg muscle).

author: RichardMCNgo
text:
Development of transistors:
Point-contact transistor (Bardeen and Brattain, 1947)
Junction transistor (Shockley, 1948 - apparently spurred by jealousy of his teammates Bardeen and Brattain)
Silicon transistor (Tanenbaum, 1955 - replacing previous use of germanium)

author: RichardMCNgo
text: How to improve the world: replace all philosophers with legal theorists. They do the same sort of conceptual analysis, but lawyers aren't hamstrung by trying to find "true definitions" - instead they merely want useful ones. Also they make fewer dodgy metaphysical assumptions.

author: RichardMCNgo
text: @cwbakerlee @Cullen_OK @Ilex_ulmus @gmiller Isn't it just a trade-off between sensory reaction times and motor reaction times though? Chest is further from eyes, closer to body. Why would the former effect be bigger?

author: RichardMCNgo
text: Why didn't we evolve to have our brains encased in our chests? Many advantages: less vulnerable, closer to blood supply, closer to muscles, makes head more maneuverable. Yet I can't think of any animals like this, so it must have major downsides. Longer optic nerves, perhaps?

author: RichardMCNgo
text: This is the *most* valuable type of thinking: trying to understand what it's like to make simple yet powerful conceptual advances that break out of existing frameworks.

quoted.text: Imagine you're a designer or mathematician living in ancient Rome. Being a curious & imaginative sort, used to exploring wild ideas, you ask yourself: is there some way you can improve on the roman numeral system? Might it be possible to find a better way of representing number?

author: RichardMCNgo
text:
A path to happiness:
1. Try everything others prioritise (money, fame, etc)
2. Realise you're still discontented.
3. Shift focus to your internal attitude.

Steps 1 and 2 not necessary, but helpful. So DM me if you're Twitter-famous and want to showcase how boring you are IRL.

author: RichardMCNgo
text: An exercise that still amazes me: start talking about anything. As you do, realise that you're not planning these particular words, they just happen, and you have no real introspective access to the underlying generators. Your thinking is a black box even to yourself.
